name: Jollof Rice
description: A vibrant and flavorful one-pot dish made with rice, tomatoes, and a blend of spices. Jollof rice is a beloved West African staple, often served at celebrations and gatherings. The rice is cooked in a rich tomato sauce infused with onions, garlic, and a variety of seasonings, resulting in a deliciously aromatic and colorful meal.
instructions: Rinse rice under cold water and set aside.
Heat oil in a pot over medium heat.
Add chopped onions; sauté until translucent.
Add tomato paste and blended tomatoes; cook until the sauce thickens.
Pour in water or stock; bring to a boil.
Add rice and seasonings; reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer until rice is cooked through (about 20–25 minutes).
Fluff with a fork and serve hot.
author: API Food Database

name: Fried Rice
description: A colorful Nigerian rice dish cooked with mixed vegetables, savory spices, and tender protein for a festive, flavorful meal
instructions: Cook rice until just done; rinse under cold water to stop cooking.
Heat oil in a large pan or wok.
Add mixed vegetables and stir‑fry for 3 minutes.
Add beef (if using) and cook until lightly browned.
Add rice and soy sauce; stir to combine evenly.
Cook for 5–7 minutes until heated through.
Adjust seasoning and serve.
author: API Food Database

name: Egusi Soup
description: A rich Nigerian soup made with ground melon seeds, leafy greens, assorted meats, and spices simmered into a hearty, comforting dish.
instructions: Rinse and grind egusi seeds to a fine powder.
Heat palm oil in a pot until hot.
Add chopped onions and sauté until fragrant.
Add egusi powder; stir often until it forms a thick paste.
Add water or stock and bring to a simmer.
Add catfish pieces; cook 15–20 minutes until fish is tender.
Add spinach; cook for another 5 minutes.
Serve with pounded yam or rice.
author: API Food Database

name: Nsala (White Soup)
description: A light and flavorful Nigerian soup made with catfish, yam paste, and aromatic spices, often enjoyed with pounded yam or fufu.
instructions: Clean catfish and slice into pieces.
Boil water with pepper and onions until aromatic.
Add catfish; simmer gently for 20–25 minutes.
Stir in yam paste to thicken slightly.
Add uziza leaves; cook for 5 more minutes.
Serve hot with yam or pounded yam.
author: API Food Database

name: Nkwobi
description: A spicy Nigerian delicacy made with tender cow foot, palm oil, and a blend of traditional spices, often enjoyed as a flavorful snack or appetizer.
instructions: Boil cow foot with seasoning until tender (about 30 minutes).
Mix potash with palm oil to create a thickened sauce.
Add boiled cow foot and pepper; stir well.
Garnish with torn utazi leaves.
Serve warm as a snack.
author: API Food Database

name: Akara
description: A popular Nigerian snack made from blended black‑eyed beans, onions, and peppers, deep-fried into crispy, golden fritters that are perfect for breakfast or as a savory treat.
instructions: Soak beans in water; peel off skins.
Blend soaked beans with onion and pepper to a smooth paste.
Heat palm oil in a deep pan.
Scoop spoonfuls of the batter into hot oil.
Fry until golden brown on all sides.
Remove; drain on paper towels and serve.
author: API Food Database

name: Pounded Yam
instructions: Peel and cut yam into chunks.
Boil in salted water until soft.
Pound with mortar/pestle until smooth and stretchy.
Serve immediately with your choice of soup.
author: API Food Database

name: Moi Moi
description: A savory Nigerian steamed bean pudding made from blended black‑eyed beans, onions, peppers, and optional eggs, cooked in banana leaves or molds for a deliciously moist and flavorful dish.
instructions: Soak beans; peel off skins.
Blend beans with onions and pepper to a smooth batter.
Stir in eggs and a little oil.
Pour mixture into molds.
Steam for 45–50 minutes until set.
Cool slightly and serve.
author: API Food Database

name: Suya
description: A popular Nigerian street food consisting of skewered and grilled meat, typically beef, coated in a spicy peanut‑based suya spice blend, often served with sliced onions and extra spice for a flavorful and satisfying snack.
instructions: Cut beef into thin strips.
Season evenly with suya spice.
Brush lightly with oil.
Grill or roast on skewers until cooked through.
Serve hot with onions and extra spice.
author: API Food Database

name: Pepper Soup
description: A spicy Nigerian soup made with tender goat meat, aromatic pepper soup spices, and a touch of bitterness from utazi leaves, simmered to perfection for a comforting and flavorful meal.
instructions: Place goat meat and water in a pot; bring to a boil.
Lower heat and simmer until meat is tender (20–25 minutes).
Add pepper soup spice; stir and cook for another 5 minutes.
Add utazi leaves; simmer briefly.
Serve hot.
author: API Food Database

name: Ofe Onugbu (Bitter Leaf Soup)
description: A rich and hearty Igbo soup made with washed bitter leaves, cocoyam paste, palm oil, and assorted meats. This traditional delicacy is known for its bold, earthy flavor and thick consistency, best enjoyed with pounded yam or fufu.
instructions: Wash bitter leaves thoroughly to reduce bitterness.
Boil assorted meat and stockfish until tender.
Add palm oil and bring to a simmer.
Stir in cocoyam paste to thicken the soup.
Add bitter leaves and cook for 10 minutes.
Season with salt, pepper, and crayfish.
Serve hot with pounded yam or fufu.
author: API Food Database

name: Banga Soup
description: A Delta State delicacy made from fresh palm fruit extract, aromatic spices, and assorted seafood or meat. Banga soup has a uniquely rich and fragrant taste from banga spices and is traditionally served with starch or pounded yam.
instructions: Boil palm fruit until soft; pound and extract juice.
Strain palm fruit extract into a pot.
Bring to a boil and add catfish pieces.
Add banga spice, onion, and seasoning.
Simmer for 20-25 minutes until thick.
Add scent leaves and cook for 5 more minutes.
Serve with starch or pounded yam.
author: API Food Database

name: Ogbono Soup
description: A thick and nutritious Nigerian soup made from ground ogbono seeds that draw naturally, creating a unique stretchy texture. Cooked with palm oil, assorted meats, and leafy greens for a hearty and satisfying meal.
instructions: Heat palm oil in a pot until hot.
Add ground ogbono; stir until it dissolves in the oil.
Add water or stock gradually, stirring constantly.
Add cooked beef and crayfish.
Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add spinach and cook for 5 more minutes.
Serve with eba, pounded yam, or rice.
author: API Food Database

name: Efo Riro
description: A vibrant Yoruba stewed spinach dish cooked with palm oil, assorted proteins, peppers, and crayfish. Efo Riro is a protein-rich and flavorful vegetable soup that pairs perfectly with any Nigerian swallow.
instructions: Blend tatashe and peppers; set aside.
Heat palm oil in a pot until hot.
Add blended peppers and fry for 10 minutes.
Add assorted meat and crayfish; stir well.
Cook for another 10 minutes until oil floats.
Add spinach and stir gently.
Cook for 5 minutes and serve.
author: API Food Database

name: Afang Soup
description: A premium Cross River and Akwa Ibom soup made with thinly sliced afang leaves and waterleaf, cooked with assorted meats, seafood, palm oil, and periwinkle. Known for its rich texture and deep flavor.
instructions: Cook assorted meat until tender; set aside.
Heat palm oil in a pot.
Add cooked meat, crayfish, and seasoning.
Add waterleaf and stir well.
Add sliced afang leaves; mix thoroughly.
Add periwinkle and cook for 10 minutes.
Serve with pounded yam or eba.
author: API Food Database

name: Edikang Ikong
description: A nutritious and prestigious Efik soup from Cross River State made with fluted pumpkin leaves, waterleaf, assorted meats, and seafood. Rich in vitamins and deeply flavorful.
instructions: Boil assorted meats until tender.
Heat palm oil in a pot.
Add meat, crayfish, and seasoning.
Add waterleaf and stir for 5 minutes.
Add ugwu leaves; mix gently.
Add periwinkle; cook for 10 minutes.
Serve with pounded yam or starch.
author: API Food Database

name: Oha Soup
description: A traditional Igbo soup made with fresh oha leaves, cocoyam paste as thickener, palm oil, and assorted meats. The delicate flavor of oha leaves makes this soup uniquely aromatic and satisfying.
instructions: Cook assorted meat until tender.
Melt cocoyam paste into the meat stock.
Add palm oil and bring to a boil.
Add crayfish and seasoning; stir well.
Simmer for 15 minutes until thickened.
Add oha leaves and cook for 5 minutes.
Serve with pounded yam or eba.
author: API Food Database

name: Ofada Stew
description: A bold and spicy Yoruba stew made with unripe tatashe, fermented locust beans, palm oil, and assorted meats. This pungent and deeply flavored stew is the perfect companion for ofada rice.
instructions: Blend tatashe and scotch bonnet; set aside.
Heat palm oil until hot.
Add iru and fry for 2 minutes.
Add blended pepper and fry for 15 minutes.
Add assorted meat and seasoning.
Cook for another 15 minutes until oil floats.
Serve with ofada rice or white rice.
author: API Food Database

name: Abacha (African Salad)
description: A popular Igbo cold dish made from shredded dried cassava, palm oil, ugba, garden eggs, and crayfish. Abacha is a uniquely tangy and flavorful snack or appetizer enjoyed across Eastern Nigeria.
instructions: Soak dried cassava in warm water for 10 minutes; drain.
Mix palm oil with potash to form a yellow paste.
Toss cassava in the palm oil mixture.
Add ugba, crayfish, and sliced garden egg.
Season with salt and pepper.
Mix well and garnish with garden eggs.
Serve cold or at room temperature.
author: API Food Database

name: Gbegiri Soup
description: A smooth and creamy Yoruba bean soup made from peeled brown beans cooked until soft and blended into a velvety consistency. Often served alongside ewedu and stew over amala for the classic abula combination.
instructions: Soak beans overnight; peel off skins.
Boil beans with onion until very soft.
Blend or mash until smooth.
Return to pot; add palm oil and crayfish.
Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring often.
Season to taste.
Serve with amala, ewedu, and stew.
author: API Food Database

name: Chicken Stir Fry
description: A quick and healthy stir fry with tender chicken strips, colorful vegetables, and a savory soy-based sauce. Ready in under 30 minutes and packed with protein and nutrients.
instructions: Slice chicken into thin strips; season lightly.
Heat oil in a wok or pan on high heat.
Add garlic and fry for 30 seconds.
Add chicken; stir fry until cooked through.
Add vegetables and stir fry for 3-4 minutes.
Add soy sauce; toss everything together.
Serve immediately with rice or noodles.
author: API Food Database

name: Grilled Chicken and Chips
description: Juicy marinated grilled chicken served alongside crispy golden potato chips. A crowd-pleasing meal that is simple to prepare and satisfying for the whole family.
instructions: Marinate chicken with spices, garlic, and oil for 30 minutes.
Peel and slice potatoes into strips.
Grill or bake chicken at 180°C for 35-40 minutes.
Deep fry potato chips until golden and crispy.
Drain chips on paper towels.
Serve chicken alongside chips with coleslaw.
author: API Food Database

name: Vegetable Omelette
description: A fluffy and nutritious egg omelette filled with sautéed vegetables, peppers, and onions. A perfect quick breakfast or light meal that is ready in under 20 minutes.
instructions: Beat eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Dice onion, tomato, and green pepper.
Heat butter in a non-stick pan.
Sauté vegetables for 2 minutes.
Pour in beaten eggs; cook on low heat.
Fold omelette in half when almost set.
Serve immediately with bread or toast.
author: API Food Database

name: Chicken Curry and Rice
description: A fragrant and mildly spiced chicken curry made with coconut milk or tomatoes, served over fluffy white rice. A popular continental dish that Nigerians have adopted and made their own.
instructions: Season and brown chicken pieces in oil.
Add diced onion; sauté until soft.
Stir in curry powder and tomato paste.
Add water or stock; bring to a boil.
Simmer for 25 minutes until chicken is tender.
Cook rice separately.
Serve curry over rice.
author: API Food Database

name: Coleslaw
description: A creamy and crunchy Nigerian-style coleslaw made with shredded cabbage, carrots, and a sweet mayonnaise dressing. A popular side dish at parties and gatherings.
instructions: Shred cabbage thinly with a knife or grater.
Grate or julienne carrots.
Mix mayonnaise, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Toss cabbage and carrots in the dressing.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes before serving.
Serve as a side dish.
author: API Food Database

name: Beef Burger
description: Juicy homemade beef patties seasoned with spices and grilled to perfection, served in soft burger buns with fresh lettuce, tomato, and condiments. A fun and satisfying meal for the whole family.
instructions: Season minced beef with spices and salt.
Shape into 4 equal patties.
Grill or pan fry patties for 5-6 minutes each side.
Toast burger buns lightly.
Assemble with lettuce, tomato, and ketchup.
Serve immediately.
author: API Food Database

name: Pancakes
description: Light and fluffy homemade pancakes made with simple pantry ingredients. Perfect for breakfast or brunch, served with honey, syrup, or fresh fruit.
instructions: Mix flour, sugar, and a pinch of salt.
Whisk eggs and milk together.
Combine wet and dry ingredients until smooth.
Heat a pan with a little butter.
Pour batter and cook until bubbles form.
Flip and cook the other side.
Serve with honey or syrup.
author: API Food Database

name: Chicken Shawarma
description: A popular street food wrap filled with spiced grilled chicken, crispy coleslaw, sliced tomatoes, and creamy garlic sauce rolled in soft flatbread. A Nigerian favourite that never gets old.
instructions: Marinate chicken in shawarma spice for 30 minutes.
Grill or pan fry chicken until cooked through.
Slice chicken into strips.
Warm flatbread slightly.
Layer chicken, coleslaw, and garlic sauce on bread.
Roll tightly and wrap in foil.
Serve immediately.
author: API Food Database

name: Spaghetti Bolognese
description: A classic Italian-inspired pasta dish with a rich and meaty tomato sauce made from minced beef, tomatoes, and aromatic herbs. A favourite in Nigerian homes for its simplicity and satisfying taste.
instructions: Boil spaghetti in salted water until al dente; drain.
Heat oil in a pan; fry onions until soft.
Add minced beef; cook until browned.
Stir in tomato paste and seasoning.
Add water and simmer for 20 minutes.
Toss spaghetti in the sauce.
Serve hot with grated cheese if desired.
author: API Food Database

name: Vegetable Fried Rice
description: A healthy and colorful fried rice packed with mixed vegetables, eggs, and a light soy sauce seasoning. A lighter vegetarian alternative to Nigerian fried rice that is quick and easy to make.
instructions: Use day-old cooked rice for best results.
Heat oil in a wok on high heat.
Scramble eggs and set aside.
Add vegetables; stir fry for 3 minutes.
Add rice; stir fry for 5 minutes.
Add soy sauce and scrambled eggs; toss together.
Serve immediately.
author: API Food Database

name: Ewa Agoyin
description: A beloved Lagos street food classic — soft mashed honey beans served with a deeply caramelized and spicy pepper sauce. Best enjoyed with agege bread for a filling and satisfying meal.
instructions: Soak beans overnight; drain and rinse.
Cook beans until very soft and mashable.
Mash beans partially — some texture is ideal.
Heat palm oil until very hot and dark.
Add sliced onions; fry until almost burnt.
Add dry pepper and fry for 10 minutes.
Serve mashed beans topped with pepper sauce and bread.
author: API Food Database

name: Nigerian Tomato Stew with Chicken
description: A rich and versatile Nigerian tomato stew made with blended tomatoes, tatashe, peppers, and tender chicken pieces. The base stew every Nigerian kitchen relies on — pairs perfectly with rice, yam, or bread.
instructions: Season and fry chicken until golden; set aside.
Blend tomatoes, tatashe, and peppers.
Heat oil in a pot; fry onions until soft.
Add blended tomatoes; cook for 20 minutes until dry.
Add chicken and seasoning; stir well.
Simmer for 15 minutes until oil floats.
Serve with white rice or boiled yam.
author: API Food Database

name: Ofada Rice and Ayamase Stew
description: A bold and distinctive Nigerian dish featuring unpolished ofada rice paired with the famous green ayamase stew made from bleached palm oil, unripe peppers, iru, and assorted meats. A true party favourite.
instructions: Wash and cook ofada rice until done; set aside.
Blend green peppers and scotch bonnet.
Bleach palm oil until clear in color.
Add iru and fry for 2 minutes.
Add blended pepper; fry for 20 minutes.
Add assorted meat and seasoning.
Serve stew over ofada rice wrapped in banana leaf.
author: API Food Database

name: Coconut Rice
description: Fragrant and creamy Nigerian coconut rice cooked in rich coconut milk with a blend of spices and optional chicken or shrimp. A stylish and aromatic one-pot rice dish perfect for any occasion.
instructions: Season and fry chicken until golden; set aside.
Sauté onions in a pot until soft.
Add washed rice; stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and water to cover rice.
Add chicken, scotch bonnet, and seasoning.
Cover and cook on low heat until rice is done.
Fluff and serve hot.
author: API Food Database

name: Nigerian Beans Porridge
description: A comforting and nutritious Nigerian one-pot dish of soft-cooked brown beans with ripe plantain, palm oil, and spices. High in protein and fiber — a complete and satisfying meal on its own.
instructions: Soak beans for 30 minutes; drain.
Boil beans until halfway cooked.
Add palm oil, onion, crayfish, and seasoning.
Peel and add plantain pieces.
Cook until beans and plantain are tender.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot.
author: API Food Database

name: Yam and Egg Sauce
description: A simple and beloved Nigerian breakfast of boiled yam served with a spicy tomato and egg sauce. Quick to prepare and deeply satisfying — a staple in every Nigerian home.
instructions: Peel and slice yam into rounds.
Boil yam in salted water until tender; drain.
Blend tomatoes, onion, and pepper.
Heat oil; fry blended tomatoes for 10 minutes.
Beat eggs and pour into the sauce.
Stir and cook until eggs are set.
Serve egg sauce over boiled yam.
author: API Food Database

name: Bole and Fish
description: A popular Nigerian street food from Rivers State — roasted unripe plantain served with grilled fish and a spicy pepper sauce. Smoky, satisfying, and completely irresistible.
instructions: Peel plantain and brush lightly with oil.
Roast plantain over open flame or grill until charred.
Season fish with salt, pepper, and spices.
Grill fish until cooked through.
Blend peppers and onion; fry briefly in oil.
Serve roasted plantain with grilled fish and pepper sauce.
author: API Food Database

name: Plantain and Egg Stir Fry
description: A quick and delicious Nigerian breakfast combining sweet fried ripe plantain with scrambled eggs, peppers, and onions. Ready in under 20 minutes and packed with energy to start the day.
instructions: Peel and slice plantain into rounds.
Fry plantain in oil until golden on both sides; set aside.
In same pan sauté onion and pepper for 2 minutes.
Beat eggs and pour in; scramble gently.
Add fried plantain back; stir together.
Season and serve immediately.
author: API Food Database

name: Yam Pottage (Asaro)
description: A creamy and comforting Nigerian yam pottage cooked in a spiced tomato and palm oil sauce until the yam is soft and slightly mashed. A one-pot meal that is simple, hearty, and deeply satisfying.
instructions: Peel and cut yam into chunks.
Boil yam with onion until halfway cooked.
Add palm oil, blended tomatoes, and crayfish.
Season with salt and pepper.
Cook until yam is soft and sauce thickens.
Mash some yam pieces for creamy texture.
Serve hot.
author: API Food Database

name: Plantain Porridge
description: A sweet and savory Nigerian plantain porridge cooked with ripe plantain, palm oil, crayfish, and leafy greens. A quick and satisfying one-pot meal that is naturally sweet and filling.
instructions: Peel and slice plantain into rounds.
Add plantain to a pot with water and onion.
Add palm oil and crayfish; bring to a boil.
Cook for 20 minutes until plantain softens.
Mash some pieces lightly for thickness.
Add spinach; cook for 5 minutes.
Serve hot.
author: API Food Database

name: Indomie Stir Fry
description: A Nigerian staple — spiced instant noodles stir fried with eggs, vegetables, and sausage for a quick, filling, and delicious meal. The ultimate comfort food ready in under 20 minutes.
instructions: Boil noodles for 2 minutes; drain and set aside.
Heat oil in a pan; fry sausage until browned.
Add vegetables; stir fry for 2 minutes.
Push to the side; scramble eggs in the pan.
Add noodles and seasoning sachets.
Toss everything together for 3 minutes.
Serve immediately.
author: API Food Database

name: Kilishi
description: A Northern Nigerian delicacy of thin spiced dried beef marinated in a rich groundnut and spice paste then sun-dried or oven-dried to perfection. A protein-packed snack with bold, complex flavors.
instructions: Slice beef very thinly against the grain.
Mix groundnut paste with suya spice, ginger, and garlic.
Coat beef slices evenly in the spice mixture.
Spread on a rack and sun-dry for 6-8 hours or oven-dry at 70°C.
Halfway through, flip and re-coat with spice.
Dry until beef is firm and leathery.
Serve as a snack or appetizer.
author: API Food Database

name: Gizdodo
description: A popular Nigerian party appetizer combining tender seasoned chicken gizzard with sweet fried ripe plantain in a spicy pepper sauce. A perfect balance of savory and sweet in every bite.
instructions: Season and cook gizzard until tender.
Fry gizzard until slightly crispy; set aside.
Slice plantain and fry until golden; set aside.
Blend tatashe and pepper; fry in oil for 10 minutes.
Add gizzard and plantain to the sauce.
Toss gently and cook for 5 minutes.
Serve as appetizer or side dish.
author: API Food Database

name: Nigerian Spring Rolls
description: Crispy golden Nigerian-style spring rolls filled with a spiced minced meat and vegetable filling, deep fried to perfection. A crowd-pleasing party snack that disappears fast.
instructions: Fry minced meat with onion and spices until cooked.
Add vegetables; stir fry for 3 minutes.
Allow filling to cool completely.
Place filling on pastry sheet and roll tightly.
Seal edges with flour paste.
Deep fry in hot oil until golden and crispy.
Drain and serve with pepper sauce.
author: API Food Database

name: Puff Puff
description: A beloved Nigerian deep-fried dough snack that is soft, fluffy, and slightly sweet inside with a golden crispy exterior. A staple at every Nigerian party and gathering.
instructions: Mix flour, sugar, yeast, and a pinch of salt.
Add warm water gradually to form a thick batter.
Cover and let rise for 45-60 minutes.
Heat oil in a deep pot.
Scoop batter with a spoon into hot oil.
Fry until golden brown on all sides.
Drain and serve warm.
author: API Food Database

name: Ogi and Akara
description: A classic Nigerian breakfast combination of smooth and creamy corn porridge served alongside crispy golden bean fritters. Light, nutritious, and comforting — a perfect way to start the day.
instructions: Mix corn flour with cold water to a smooth paste.
Pour into boiling water; stir constantly until thick.
Sweeten ogi to taste; set aside.
Soak and blend beans with onion and pepper.
Deep fry spoonfuls of bean batter until golden.
Drain akara on paper towels.
Serve ogi in bowls alongside hot akara.
author: API Food Database

name: Okpa
description: A beloved Enugu State delicacy made from ground bambara nuts steamed in banana leaves or nylon bags. Dense, protein-rich, and deeply satisfying — often enjoyed as breakfast or a filling snack.
instructions: Mix okpa flour with palm oil until combined.
Add pepper, crayfish, onion, and salt.
Add warm water gradually to form a thick batter.
Pour batter into nylon bags or banana leaf wraps.
Seal and steam for 45-60 minutes.
Allow to cool slightly before unwrapping.
Serve warm.
author: API Food Database

name: Nigerian Coconut Jollof Rice
description: A fragrant and luxurious twist on classic jollof rice, cooked in a blend of tomato sauce and creamy coconut milk for a rich, aromatic, and slightly sweet flavor profile. Elegant enough for any occasion.
instructions: Season and fry chicken until golden; set aside.
Blend tomatoes and peppers; fry in oil for 15 minutes.
Add coconut milk; stir and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add washed rice and chicken.
Pour in water to cover; season well.
Cover and cook on low heat until rice is done.
Serve hot garnished with fresh herbs.
author: API Food Database

name: Concoction Rice
description: A rustic and deeply flavorful Nigerian one-pot rice dish cooked with palm oil, crayfish, vegetables, and fish or meat. Every household has their own version — simple, economical, and completely delicious.
instructions: Wash rice and set aside.
Heat palm oil in a pot; add crayfish and fry briefly.
Add rice and stir to coat in oil.
Add water to cover; season well.
Add smoked fish and bring to a boil.
Cook on low heat until rice is almost done.
Add vegetables; cover and steam for 5 minutes.
author: API Food Database

name: Seafood Okra Rice
description: A bold and flavorful Nigerian rice dish cooked with fresh okra, assorted seafood, palm oil, and spices. The okra gives the rice a naturally thick and slightly sticky texture that is uniquely satisfying.
instructions: Wash and slice okra finely; set aside.
Cook seafood briefly with seasoning; set aside.
Heat palm oil; add crayfish and fry briefly.
Add washed rice; stir to coat.
Add water and seafood stock; bring to a boil.
Cook rice until almost done.
Add okra and seafood; cover and steam for 10 minutes.
author: API Food Database

name: Tomato Rice with Chicken
description: A simple, flavorful Nigerian tomato rice cooked in a light tomato sauce with tender chicken pieces and aromatic spices. A lighter alternative to jollof rice that is quick and satisfying.
instructions: Season and fry chicken until golden; set aside.
Sauté onions in oil until soft.
Add tomato paste; fry for 5 minutes.
Add washed rice; stir to combine.
Add water and chicken; season well.
Cover and cook on low heat until rice is done.
Serve hot.
author: API Food Database

name: Ofada Rice with Egg Sauce
description: Nutty and aromatic unpolished ofada rice served with a spiced tomato and egg sauce. A simple but deeply satisfying everyday meal that highlights the natural flavor of Nigeria's beloved local rice.
instructions: Wash ofada rice thoroughly; cook until done.
Blend tomatoes and onion; fry in oil for 10 minutes.
Add seasoning and scotch bonnet.
Beat eggs; pour into sauce.
Stir and cook until eggs are set.
Serve egg sauce over ofada rice.
author: API Food Database

name: Nigerian Omelette and Bread
description: A thick and spicy Nigerian-style omelette loaded with peppers, onions, and tomatoes, served alongside soft agege bread. The ultimate quick Nigerian breakfast that is filling and delicious.
instructions: Dice tomato, onion, and scotch bonnet.
Beat eggs with a pinch of salt.
Heat oil in a pan; sauté vegetables for 1 minute.
Pour in beaten eggs.
Cook on low heat without stirring.
Fold when top is almost set.
Serve with agege bread.
author: API Food Database

name: Masa with Miyan Taushe
description: A Northern Nigerian specialty of soft and spongy fermented rice cakes served with a rich and spiced pumpkin soup. A complete and satisfying meal that showcases the depth of Hausa cuisine.
instructions: Mix rice flour with water to a smooth batter; ferment overnight.
Cook masa in a greased special pan or non-stick pan.
Blend tomatoes and peppers for the soup.
Fry blended tomatoes in oil for 10 minutes.
Add meat and pumpkin; cook until tender.
Season to taste.
Serve masa with miyan taushe.
author: API Food Database

name: Nigerian Pepper Chicken
description: Tender chicken pieces cooked in a bold and fiery Nigerian pepper sauce made from blended scotch bonnet, tatashe, and onions. A spicy and aromatic dish that pairs perfectly with rice, yam, or bread.
instructions: Season chicken and boil until cooked through.
Blend scotch bonnet, tatashe, and onion.
Fry chicken in oil until golden; set aside.
In same oil fry blended pepper for 15 minutes.
Add chicken back to the pepper sauce.
Stir and cook for 10 minutes until flavors merge.
Serve with rice or yam.
author: API Food Database

name: Miyan Kuka
description: A traditional Northern Nigerian soup made from dried and ground baobab leaves cooked with palm oil, meat, and spices. Miyan Kuka has a distinctive earthy flavor and slimy texture, best enjoyed with tuwo shinkafa or eba.
instructions: Cook meat until tender; set aside with stock.
Heat palm oil in a pot.
Add onion and crayfish; fry for 2 minutes.
Add meat and stock; bring to a boil.
Sprinkle in baobab leaf powder gradually while stirring.
Cook for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Season to taste and serve with tuwo shinkafa.
author: API Food Database

name: Okra Soup
description: A thick and hearty Nigerian okra soup made with freshly sliced okra, palm oil, assorted meats, and seafood. The natural drawing quality of okra creates a uniquely satisfying texture loved across all Nigerian tribes.
instructions: Cook assorted meat until tender; set aside.
Slice okra finely or blend roughly.
Heat palm oil in a pot.
Add crayfish and pepper; fry for 2 minutes.
Add meat and stock; bring to a boil.
Add sliced okra; stir and cook for 10 minutes.
Serve with eba, pounded yam, or rice.
author: API Food Database

name: Groundnut Soup
description: A rich and creamy Northern Nigerian soup made from roasted groundnut paste simmered with chicken, tomatoes, and aromatic spices. Nutty, hearty, and deeply satisfying — best served over rice or with tuwo.
instructions: Season and brown chicken in a pot.
Add blended tomatoes, onion, and pepper.
Cook for 15 minutes until tomatoes dry.
Dilute groundnut paste with water; add to pot.
Stir well and simmer for 20 minutes.
Season to taste.
Serve over rice or with tuwo shinkafa.

name: Fisherman Soup

Spread suya butter generously between each cut.
Spoon caramelized onions between each cut pressing gently.
Tuck grated cheese between each cut on top of the onions.
Wrap the whole loaf in foil; bake for 15 minutes.
Unwrap foil for the last 5 minutes to crisp and brown the top.
Serve immediately — pull apart to eat.

name: Yam and Avocado Bowl
description: A beautiful and nutritious Nigerian bowl featuring golden baked yam wedges served over a creamy avocado mash with a spiced tomato salsa and crayfish drizzle. A modern, health-conscious, and completely satisfying standalone meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C; line a baking tray with foil.
Peel yam and cut into thick wedges; toss with oil, salt, and a pinch of mixed spice.
Arrange yam wedges on baking tray; bake for 20-25 minutes flipping once until golden and tender.
While yam bakes prepare avocado mash: scoop avocado flesh into a bowl.
Mash with a fork until creamy; add lime juice, salt, and a tiny pinch of scotch bonnet.
For spiced tomato salsa: finely dice tomato, onion, and scotch bonnet.
Mix together with a squeeze of lime juice and salt; stir in crayfish.
Let salsa sit for 5 minutes for flavors to develop.
Assemble bowls: spread avocado mash generously as the base.
Arrange hot baked yam wedges on top of the avocado.
Spoon spiced tomato and crayfish salsa over the yam.
Serve immediately — the contrast of warm yam with cool avocado is the magic.
